title: Luna 2x Telescope Knights

sources.label: NEW ★★★ Luna 2x Telescope RAMPAGE Build For Dota Auto Chess

body:
# Luna 2x Telescope Knights

This is a Knights board that exists to feed one carry: a three-star Luna wearing
two Telescopes. Telescope is only a tier-two item, but it grants Luna +200 attack
range and, critically, scales her physical damage by how far her projectiles
travel — so from the back corner of a max-range board her glaives (and their
bounces) hit for enormous numbers, and she racks up rampage after rampage. A
two-cost unit at three stars normally falls off hard after round 30; the double
Telescope is what keeps Luna relevant into the ultra-late game. The Knight and
Troll bodies around her exist to buy time, shield her, and later pivot into Naga
for magic resistance once the lobby turns into mages.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Luna | 2 | Elf, Knight | The carry — three-star her and stack two Telescopes plus a damage/lifesteal item |
| Chaos Knight | 2 | Demon, Knight | Frontline tank and second three-star priority; great Aegis holder |
| Batrider | 2 | Knight, Troll | Bridges both bonds (counts as Knight *and* Troll); solid frontline body |
| Troll Warlord | 5 | Troll, Warrior | Late Troll upgrade; strong attack-speed body |
| Huskar | 3 | Troll, Warrior | Troll filler with built-in magic resist as it drops low |
| Shadow Shaman | 1 | Shaman, Troll | Cheap Troll body (do not waste rolls three-starring it) |
| Witch Doctor | 1 | Troll, Warlock | Cheap Troll body |
| Dazzle | 1 | Priest, Troll | Cheap Troll body; a three-star Dazzle prolongs fights with heals |
| Medusa | 4 | Hunter, Naga | Late-game stone/stun layer and Naga magic resist |
| Naga Siren | 3 | Naga, Wizard | Second Naga for the 15% team magic resist vs mages |

The spine is 6 Troll (Shadow Shaman, Witch Doctor, Dazzle, Batrider, Huskar,
Troll Warlord) plus 4 Knight (Luna, Chaos Knight, Batrider, and a fourth such as
Snapfire), with two Naga bolted on late for the mage matchup. Batrider doing
double duty is what makes both bonds affordable at once.

## Items

The whole build hinges on finding **two Telescopes** — one is not enough, and if
Luna doesn't have both by round 30 the board falls off a cliff. If you can't find
the second naturally, hold a **Sliver** and reroll it into Telescope, or use a
consumable relic to downgrade a tier-three item back into a tier-two roll. Once
the Telescopes are online, Luna wants raw damage and survivability: **Daedalus**
(the reliable default), **Satanic** for lifesteal sustain, **Manta Style** for
two extra glaive-throwing illusions, **Black King Bar** against mage lobbies, and
**Aegis of Immortal** for a second life. Divine Rapier is the theoretical
ceiling but too risky — if Luna dies, the enemy takes it. Spare items go on the
Knights: **Aegis of Immortal** on Chaos Knight, **Drum of Endurance** on Batrider
for the team aura.

## Relics

The build wants a protected losing streak into a big level-15 roll, so the
win/lose-streak protector (Chiaroscuro Certainty) is high value — just click it
*before* the round you'd break streak, not after. **Wheel of Wonder** can gamble
for a better unit. The video also leans on a neutral "Mentor" pickup late that
copies Luna's items onto her Manta illusions; grab it if offered, since it
multiplies her whole item stack across the board.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Don't level early — bank gold on a losing streak with a Priest (and optionally a
Panda) down for income, and let your XP drift you to level 5 by round 15. Round
15 is the payoff: with 70–80 gold saved and the greedy discount unlocked, roll
hard for your three-star Trolls and Knights, prioritizing Luna, then Chaos
Knight, then Batrider and Dazzle. Dismiss Warriors early to thin the pool (accepting
that you may not see Troll Warlord or Huskar until later — that's fine, you lack
board space for them early anyway). After Luna is three-starred and Telescoped,
push levels to 10 and then 11 to add Naga and more Troll/Knight depth.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Luna belongs in a back corner at maximum distance from the enemy — that's where
her per-distance damage peaks — with Chaos Knight and Batrider planted in front
of her to soak the first wave, and the cheap bodies baiting AoE and projectiles.
Against mages (five-dragon / six or nine mage boards) she needs Black King Bar to
survive the crowd control, and the two Naga bodies plus Medusa's stone are what
let the board outlast a Dragon Mage burst. A late trick the video stresses:
against a threatening carry like a three-star Spectre, physically flipping your
board 180° to the opposite side can dodge its teleport/engage and let Luna snipe
it as it arrives — board rotation is a real lever in the ultra-late game.
